findings.detail: Two wrong options repeat wrong options of earlier questions on the same idea. Option C uses a PostToolUse hook to block a call that has already run, which repeats the PostToolUse wrong option of M1-S14-T2 and the cause in M4-S19-T1. Option D replaces the hook with a system prompt rule, which repeats the prompt wrong options of M1-S14-T2 and M1-S18-T1. The blocking half of the question therefore needs the same reasoning as M1-S14-T2: intercept the outgoing call rather than use PostToolUse or a prompt. Only option A adds a new problem, the normalization side. At most one wrong option may repeat.

blind_answer.reason: Blocking production releases has to happen before the tool runs, so it needs a hook that intercepts the outgoing deploy_service call. The date formats only show up in the tool results, so a PostToolUse hook should normalize them. A is wrong because the outgoing call contains no dates to fix. C is wrong because a PostToolUse hook runs after the deploy has already happened. D is wrong because a prompt rule is only probabilistic, not guaranteed compliance.
